inputKinds.arg: {arg:name} one input from that argument (multichannel-expandable). Optional flags: audioRate (sclang converts with asAudioRateInput, see special.asAudioRateInput), numberToImpulse (Poll trig), field (InRect: left/top/right/bottom of a Rect).
inputKinds.arrayArg: {arrayArg:name} the argument is an array whose elements become consecutive inputs (not expanded). Nested arrays inside it multichannel-expand the UGen. Optional: extendTo/pad (Dwrand weights), wrapExtend (LocalIn default, wrapped to that arg's value).
inputKinds.arrayLength: {arrayLength:name} one constant input = size of that array argument.
inputKinds.const: {const:n} constant inserted by sclang regardless of arguments.
inputKinds.ugen: {ugen:Class} input wired to an auxiliary UGen sclang creates (LocalBuf -> MaxLocalBufs).
inputKinds.env: {env:name, format:"envgen"|"ienvgen"} the Env argument flattened into inputs (see special.EnvGen / special.IEnvGen).
inputKinds.spec: {spec:name, format:"klank"|"klang"} Klank/Klang specification Ref flattened (see special).
inputKinds.string: {string:name} one input per ascii code of the String/Symbol argument; {stringLength:name} its length.

methodFields.args: sclang positional argument order (mul/add removed when mulAdd). default null = nil. "inf" = Infinity. Symbols are strings. nilMeans: what nil turns into ({arg}|{const}|{expr}); required: nil is not allowed.
methodFields.mulAdd: the constructor ends with .madd(mul, add) (see special.MulAdd for the degenerate cases); mul/add are not inputs.
methodFields.mulAddIndex: present when mul/add are not the last two positional args: index of mul in the full positional list (add follows it).
methodFields.rate: rate sclang assigns: audio|control|scalar|demand, or fromInputs.
methodFields.numOutputs: number, or {arg:name} (value of that argument), or {arrayLength:name}.
methodFields.returns: what the constructor returns when it is not the UGen: {const:0} (no usable output) or {arg:name} (returns that argument).
methodFields.bypass: constructor shortcut: if scalarArg has scalar rate (number or scalar-rate UGen) or zeroArg == 0, no UGen is made and the result is scalarArg.madd(mul, add).
methodFields.postOps: operations applied to the result instead of inputs, e.g. [{op:"*",arg:"level"}] (skipped when the arg is 1).

ugenFields.serverName: unit name written into the SynthDef (differs only for Dstutter -> Ddup).
ugenFields.pure: sclang dead-code-eliminates it when nothing reads its output (PureUGen/PureMultiOutUGen/Unary/BinaryOpUGen; DetectSilence opts out).
ugenFields.sideEffect: judgement: writes buses/buffers, sends messages, frees/pauses nodes (incl. via doneAction) or changes synth state; sclang keeps every non-pure UGen regardless.
ugenFields.widthFirst: sclang WidthFirstUGen (affects topological sort, see special.WidthFirstUGen).
ugenFields.checks: rate checks sclang applies at SynthDef build (failure = build error). audioRateInputs(i..) = those inputs must be audio rate when the UGen is audio rate.
ugenFields.specialIndex: non-zero specialIndex written for the UGen.
ugenFields.special: key(s) into the top-level special map describing extra sclang behaviour.

argDocs.freq: Frequency in Hertz. Positive frequencies only.
argDocs.width: Duty cycle, denoting where in the cycle the waveform peaks. g.

Vibrato.summary: The Vibrato oscillator models a slow frequency modulation.

argDocs.freq: Fundamental frequency in Hertz. If the Vibrato UGen is running at audio rate, this must not be a constant, but an actual audio rate UGen (see example below)
argDocs.rate: Vibrato rate, speed of wobble in Hertz. 0), you may never get vibrato back, since the rate input is only checked at the end of a cycle.
argDocs.depth: Size of vibrato frequency deviation around the fundamental, as a proportion of the fundamental. 02 = 2% of the fundamental.
argDocs.delay: Delay before vibrato is established in seconds (a singer tends to attack a note and then stabilise with vibrato, for instance).
argDocs.onset: Transition time in seconds from no vibrato to full vibrato after the initial delay time.
argDocs.rateVariation: Noise on the rate, expressed as a proportion of the rate; can change once per cycle of vibrato.
argDocs.depthVariation: Noise on the depth of modulation, expressed as a proportion of the depth; can change once per cycle of vibrato. The noise affects independently the up and the down part of vibrato shape within a cycle.
argDocs.iphase: Initial phase of vibrato modulation, allowing starting above or below the fundamental rather than on it.
argDocs.trig: Start again if transition from trig <= 0 to trig > 0.

Warp1.summary: Warp a buffer with a time pointer

argDocs.numChannels: the number of channels in the soundfile used in bufnum. Must be a nonzero, positive integer.
argDocs.bufnum: the buffer number of a mono soundfile.
argDocs.pointer: the position in the buffer. The value should be between 0 and 1, with 0 being the beginning of the buffer, and 1 the end.
argDocs.freqScale: the amount of frequency shift. 0 is one octave up.
argDocs.windowSize: the size of each grain window.
argDocs.envbufnum: the buffer number containing a signal to use for the grain envelope. -1 uses a built-in Hanning envelope.
argDocs.windowRandRatio: the amount of randomness to the windowing function. 0 (probably too random actually)
argDocs.interp: the interpolation method used for pitchshifting grains. 1 = no interpolation.

special.EnvGen: EnvGen.ar/kr(envelope, gate=1, levelScale=1, levelBias=0, timeScale=1, doneAction=0). Inputs = [gate, levelScale, levelBias, timeScale, doneAction] ++ envArray (input kind {env, format:"envgen"}). envArray = Env.asArray = [levels[0], numSegments, releaseNode ?? -99, loopNode ?? -99] then for each segment i: [levels[i+1], times[i], shapeNumber(curves.wrapAt(i)), curveValue(curves.wrapAt(i))]. Env.new wraps times to levels.size-1 and defaults curve to \lin. shapeNumber: step 0, lin/linear 1, exp/exponential 2, sin/sine 3, wel/welch 4, any number 5, sqr/squared 6, cub/cubed 7, hold 8; curveValue = the curve if it is a number/UGen, else 0. Env offset is not used. A plain Array envelope is used verbatim. If any level/time/curve is an Array the Env is multichannel (asMultichannelArray = prAsArray.flop) and one EnvGen per channel is made. Env:kr(doneAction=0, gate=1, timeScale=1, levelScale=1, levelBias=0) and Env:ar take their args in that different order and call EnvGen.
special.IEnvGen: IEnvGen.ar/kr(envelope, index, mul=1, add=0). Inputs = [index] ++ Env.asArrayForInterpolation (input kind {env, format:"ienvgen"}) = [offset ?? 0, levels[0], numSegments, sum(times)] then for each segment i: [times[i], shapeNumber(curves.wrapAt(i)), curveValue(curves.wrapAt(i)), levels[i+1]] (shape numbers as for EnvGen); multichannel Envs give one IEnvGen per channel. Then .madd(mul, add).
special.Klank: Klank.ar(specificationsArrayRef, input, freqscale=1, freqoffset=0, decayscale=1). The spec is a Ref (`[freqs, amps, ringtimes]); nil amps -> all 1.0, nil ringtimes -> all 1.0. Inputs = [input, freqscale, freqoffset, decayscale] ++ [freqs, amps, ringtimes].flop.flat, i.e. per partial: freq, amp, ringtime (input kind {spec, format:"klank"}). Multichannel: Ref.multichannelExpandRef(2) - if any value inside freqs/amps/ringtimes is itself an Array, the spec is flopDeep(2)-ed and one Klank per channel is made (channel c uses element c, wrapped, of each nested value).
special.Klang: Klang.ar(specificationsArrayRef, freqscale=1, freqoffset=0). Spec Ref `[freqs, amps, phases]; nil amps -> 1.0, nil phases -> 0.0. Inputs = [freqscale, freqoffset] ++ [freqs, amps, phases].flop.flat (per partial: freq, amp, phase). Same multichannelExpandRef(2) rule as Klank.
special.Dwrand: Dwrand(list, weights, repeats=1): inputs = [repeats, list.size] ++ weights.extend(list.size, 0.0) ++ list (weights padded with 0.0 or truncated to list.size). Demand rate.
special.Dpoll: Dpoll(in, label, run=1, trigid=-1): label = label ?? ("DemandUGen(" ++ in.class.name ++ ")"); inputs = [in, trigid, run, label.size] ++ label character codes (ascii), one input per character. Demand rate.
special.Poll: Poll.ar/kr(trig, in, label, trigid=-1), Poll(trig, in, label, trigid) and ugen.poll(trig=10, label, trigid=-1). label = label ?? ("UGen(" ++ in.class.name ++ ")") - the class of a MultiOutUGen channel is OutputProxy, giving "UGen(OutputProxy)". A number trig is replaced by Impulse.<rate>(trig, 0) (created after `in`, just before the Poll). Poll.new takes its rate from `in` (scalar -> control). Inputs = [trig, in, trigid, label.size] ++ label ascii codes. The constructor returns `in`, not the Poll.
special.SendReply: SendReply.ar/kr(trig=0, cmdName='/reply', values, replyID=-1): if values contains no nested Array it is wrapped ([values]); then [trig, cmdName, values, replyID].flop makes one SendReply per row. Each: inputs = [trig, replyID, cmdName.size] ++ cmdName ascii codes ++ values. 0 outputs; returns 0.
special.SendPeakRMS: SendPeakRMS.ar/kr(sig, replyRate=20, peakLag=3, cmdName='/reply', replyID=-1): calls new1 directly, so no multichannel expansion. Inputs = [replyRate, peakLag, replyID, sig.size] ++ sig.flatten ++ [cmdName.size] ++ cmdName ascii codes. 0 outputs; returns 0.
special.InRect: InRect.ar/kr(x=0, y=0, rect): rect is an sclang Rect(left, top, width, height); inputs = [x, y, rect.left, rect.top, rect.right (= left + width), rect.bottom (= top + height)].
special.LocalBuf: LocalBuf(numFrames=1, numChannels=1), scalar rate, WidthFirstUGen. Inputs = [numChannels, numFrames, <MaxLocalBufs>]. The first LocalBuf of a SynthDef creates one MaxLocalBufs UGen (added to the graph just before that LocalBuf); its single input is the number of LocalBufs in the def (incremented by every LocalBuf, including ones added by PV_Copy insertion), and every LocalBuf takes it as its 3rd input. LocalBuf.newFrom(list) = LocalBuf(list.size, 1) (or shape for 2-D lists) followed by SetBuf(buf, list.flop.flat, 0).
special.MaxLocalBufs: Created automatically by the first LocalBuf of a SynthDef (see LocalBuf); scalar rate, one input = total LocalBuf count. Not constructed by user code.
special.LocalIn: LocalIn.ar/kr(numChannels=1, default=0): numChannels outputs; inputs = default.asArray.wrapExtend(numChannels), one input per channel with defaults cycled (input kind {arrayArg, wrapExtend}).
special.VarLag: VarLag.ar/kr(in=0, time=0.1, curvature=0, warp=5, start, mul=1, add=0). If in.rate == scalar or time == 0: no UGen, returns in.madd(mul, add). Else start = start ? in, curve = Env.shapeNames[warp] ? warp. If curve == 1 (\lin/\linear): VarLag UGen with inputs [in, time, start] (curvature and warp are dropped). Otherwise - including the default warp=5 - it builds EnvGen.<rate>(e, trig) with e = Env([start, in], [time], warp).asArray, e[6] = curve, e[7] = curvature, trig = Changed.<rate>(in) + Impulse.<rate>(0) (+ Changed.kr(time) if time is not scalar), where Changed(x) = HPZ1.<rate>(x).abs > 0. Then .madd(mul, add).
special.Lag: Lag/Lag2/Lag3/Ramp .ar/.kr: if in.rate == scalar (a number, or a scalar-rate UGen such as Rand or an ir control) or lagTime == 0 (a literal 0), no UGen is created and the result is in.madd(mul, add) (method field "bypass"). LagUD/Lag2UD/Lag3UD/Slew do the same for scalar `in` only. The UGen methods sig.lag/lag2/lag3/lagud/slew/varlag call multiNew directly and never bypass.
special.Dstutter: Dstutter(n, in) is deprecated: it returns Ddup(n, in), so the SynthDef contains a "Ddup" unit (serverName Ddup) and the first use posts a warning.
special.Out: Out/ReplaceOut/OffsetOut/XOut/LocalOut .ar: channelsArray = UGen.replaceZeroesWithSilence(channelsArray.asUGenInput.asArray): elements equal to 0 are all replaced by ONE shared DC.ar(0) created inside the call (after the other channels, before the Out). .kr variants do not do this. Inputs = fixed args ++ channels; 0 outputs; the constructor returns 0. OffsetOut has no .kr. Nested arrays in channelsArray multichannel-expand into several Outs.
special.asAudioRateInput: Inputs marked "audioRate": true (DelayN/L/C, CombN/L/C, AllpassN/L/C, BufDelayN/L/C, BufCombN/L/C, BufAllpassN/L/C and DelTapWr, .ar only) go through asAudioRateInput: a number n becomes DC.ar(n) (0 -> DC.ar(0) via Silent.ar), a non-audio UGen u becomes K2A.ar(u); the converter is created before the UGen.
special.DemandEnvGen: DemandEnvGen.ar: if gate or reset is audio rate, the other one is wrapped in K2A.ar when it is not audio rate (K2A created before DemandEnvGen). .kr does no conversion.
special.WhiteNoise: WhiteNoise/BrownNoise/PinkNoise/ClipNoise/GrayNoise .ar/.kr: if mul is an Array, one noise UGen per mul element is created (SC2 idiom), then .madd(mul, add).
special.LinXFade2: LinXFade2.ar/kr(inA, inB=0, pan=0, level=1): level is not an input; the result is `ugen * level` (BinaryOpUGen *, skipped when level == 1) - method field "postOps".
special.DecodeB2: DecodeB2.ar/kr(numChans, w, x, y, orientation=0.5): the orientation argument is ignored - the class library passes `orientation = 0.5` (an assignment), so input 3 is always the constant 0.5.
special.PV_ChainUGen: FFT, PV_* and PackFFT are PV_ChainUGens. At SynthDef finish (addCopiesIfNeeded), if one chain UGen is an input of more than one WidthFirstUGen (other than PV_Copy), then for every such consumer except the last (graph order) sclang inserts frames = chain.fftSize (FFT: BufFrames.ir(fft.inputs[0]); PV_*: inputs[0].fftSize; PackFFT: its bufsize input), buf = LocalBuf(frames) (numChannels 1, increments MaxLocalBufs), copy = PV_Copy(chain, buf), rewires that consumer to copy, and places frames/buf/copy directly after the chain UGen.
special.WidthFirstUGen: WidthFirstUGens (FFT, IFFT, PV_*, PackFFT, LocalBuf, SetBuf, ClearBuf, RandSeed, RandID; field "widthFirst") are recorded in creation order; every UGen added after one gets all previously created WidthFirstUGens as extra antecedents for the topological sort, so they stay ahead of everything created after them.
special.BinaryOpUGen: Internal. Created by math on UGens: BinaryOpUGen(selector, a, b), specialIndex = operator index (field "operators"), rate = demand > audio > control > scalar of the two inputs. new1 folds: a*0/0*b -> 0, *1 -> other, *-1 -> other.neg, +0 -> other, 0-b -> b.neg, a-0 -> a, a/1 -> a, a/-1 -> a.neg. optimizeGraph (pure, dead-code eliminated): for +: Sum3 from (x+y)+z, Sum4 from Sum3+w, MulAdd from (x*y)+z when MulAdd.canBeMulAdd, a + b.neg -> a - b; for -: a - b.neg -> a + b; folded UGens must have exactly one descendant.
special.UnaryOpUGen: Internal. UnaryOpUGen(selector, a): specialIndex = operator index (field "operators"), rate = a.rate, pure (dead-code eliminated).
special.MulAdd: Internal (not pure: never dead-code eliminated). MulAdd(in, mul=1, add=0) / ugen.madd: mul == 0 -> add; mul == 1 && add == 0 -> in; mul == -1 && add == 0 -> in.neg; add == 0 -> in * mul; mul == -1 -> add - in; mul == 1 -> in + add; else MulAdd(in, mul, add) if canBeMulAdd(in, mul, add), else MulAdd(mul, in, add) if canBeMulAdd(mul, in, add), else (in * mul) + add. canBeMulAdd(in, mul, add) = in is audio rate, or in is control rate and mul and add are control or scalar. Rate = highest input rate.
special.Sum3: Internal. Sum3(in0, in1, in2): if any input == 0 it becomes a +; otherwise inputs are sorted by rate (sort {|a b| a.rate < b.rate}, i.e. comparing rate Symbols alphabetically: audio < control < demand < scalar).
special.Sum4: Internal. Sum4(in0..in3): if any input == 0 it becomes a Sum3; otherwise inputs sorted by rate as for Sum3.
special.Control: Internal. Control/AudioControl/TrigControl/LagControl are created by SynthDef from the ugenGraphFunc arguments (and NamedControl): one Control per rate group, specialIndex = index of its first value in the SynthDef controls array; LagControl inputs are the lag times.
